text:
maya: Heads up — dewdrop-embed-v2 int8 bring-up shows a suspicious quality regression vs baseline. Can we triage?

dev-bot: CI eval finished for dewdrop-embed-v2 (int8-per-tensor):
```
recall@1: 0.77  (-0.04 vs baseline)
recall@10: 0.93 (-0.02 vs baseline)
silhouette: 0.16 (baseline 0.21)
median cosine shift: -0.012
```

sam: I ran a quick local sweep, same direction. Distribution shifted left, median cosine difference ~0.012.

lina: :thinking_face: Are we using per-tensor or per-channel quantization for this sweep?

sam: Per-tensor. We did that for the initial fast scan. Per-channel normally helps with these transformer-sized embeddings. I'll re-run per-channel.

maya: Also please split by short vs long queries — remember short queries (<=8 tokens) were fragile in the compact experiments.

sam: Launching: `./scripts/run_embed_eval --model dewdrop-embed-v2 --quant int8 --scheme per-channel --holdout short,long --k 10 --batch 256 --seed 42`

dev-bot: Job queued (#9421) — runners: vector-eval-3

jordan: Quick reminder: baseline pipeline did mean-centering + L2 norm before index. New training pipeline might have removed centering for speed. That can explain silhouette drop.

sam: Good catch — baseline used subtract-mean + L2. I'll re-run with centering enabled in preprocessing.

lina: If per-channel + centering recovers under ~1% drop on recall and silhoutte recovers, we can accept int8 for Dedicated. Add cluster purity and pairwise delta plots to the job.

maya: Plan: sam runs per-channel + centering short/long holdouts by EOD; lina will run per-dim quant noise profiling; jordan will bisect the commit that removed centering. If metrics still bad, fallback to int4/float16 policy for the first rollout.

sam: Started runs. Will post quick results here when done.

sam: Update (results): per-channel + centering ->
```
short-holdout recall@1: 0.768 (-0.022 vs baseline)
short-holdout recall@10: 0.935 (-0.01)
long-holdout recall@1: 0.780 (-0.017)
silhouette: 0.195
median cosine shift: -0.004
```

sam: So per-channel + centering recovers most of the loss, but there's still ~1.5-2% gap on short queries. I'll run a tighter per-channel calibration (scale clipping) and produce pairwise scatter + delta histograms.

lina: Nice — can you also dump top-1 failure examples (short queries) to S3 so we can inspect semantics? Path: s3://redwood-evals/dewdrop/v2/int8-perchannel/short-failures/

sam: Done, uploaded ~150 examples. Link: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-evals/dewdrop/v2/int8-perchannel/short-failures/manifest.json

maya: Thanks everyone. If the calibration run recovers the last ~1% we greenlight int8 for prod bring-up with a canary guard. Otherwise we'll gate to float16 and continue iterate.
